review.reason: Teaches how measurement boundaries affect historical inference; explicitly an ongoing project report.

item.title: Beyond the mole: redefining harbour capacity for the ancient Mediterranean
item.headline: Ancient ports extended beyond their surviving harbour walls
item.authors: Emmanuel Nantet, Matthieu Giaime, and Michael Lazar
item.summary: A project report combines harbour basins with nearby anchorage to reassess usable capacity. Reconstructed space is not measured cargo throughput, and fieldwork continues.

evidence.question: What should count when estimating an ancient port’s capacity?
evidence.method: Comparative archaeological, sediment, mooring, and geophysical evidence across Mediterranean settings.
evidence.limitations: Uneven preservation, reconstructed depths, and unverified survey anomalies.

explainer.finding: Nearby bays and anchorage zones can materially change estimates based only on enclosed basins.
explainer.method: Researchers combine coastal reconstruction, mooring evidence, and land and marine surveys.
explainer.meaning: Counting only surviving quays resembles measuring a station by its waiting room: the boundary can miss essential operating space.
explainer.limits: This is an ongoing project’s methodological report, not a finished numerical ranking or direct measurement of ancient trade volumes.
